Based on your experience at the AP®
Reading with student responses, what advice would you offer
teachers to help them improve the student performance on the exam?
• Teachers could model precise and accurate communication, never displaying linkage errors or equating a variable
expression to a constant value. Teachers could also require such accurate communication in all student work.
• Teachers could encourage students to carefully label their work so that they are unlikely to use terms such as “it”
or “the function” in their reasoning or explanations. For example, a correct label of ( ) 2 52 m′ = makes it easier to
argue that m is increasing at 2 x = because ( ) 2 0, m′ > rather than “because it is positive.”
• Teachers could provide students with more practice finding derivatives that require use of both the product and
chain rules or the quotient and chain rules. It would also be beneficial to incorporate multiple named functions
such as ( ) ( ) ( ) ( ) 2
k x h x g x = ⋅ or ( )

• Teachers could provide students with opportunities to compare and contrast functions that may at first look
similar. For example, compare the following: ( ) ( ) ( )

What resources would you recommend to teachers to better prepare their students for the content
and skill(s) required on this question?
• This question requires identification (skill 1.C or 1.D) and application (skill 1.E) of appropriate mathematical
rules and procedures. Most parts also involve identifying mathematical information from the given table, a
numerical representation of functions (skill 2.B). To earn all points, responses must clearly present the use of the
relevant rule(s). That is, points are not typically earned without supporting work. Relevant topics include 2.8, 3.1,
and 6.7. AP Daily videos for each of these Topics provide guidance on how to show supporting work.
• It is typically necessary to show enough work that the form of the relevant derivative or integral is evident. The
scoring notes for part (b) to this question illustrate several expressions containing a single error that would
nonetheless earn the first point for showing the form of either the product rule or the chain rule. Model solutions,
scoring notes, and Chief Reader Reports for past exam questions are excellent resources to help students to
develop understanding and mastery.
